correctness.rationale: The crown neighborhood formulas reduce the definition to exact interval inequalities in the two side sums. Weights below six are excluded by analyzing a zero coordinate on a side of weight at most two. At weight six, side weights below three are impossible, so both side sums equal three. The interval constraints then force coordinatewise equality across every deleted pair. Every common side vector of sum three is feasible, proving the value, classification, and count. The package checker independently exhausts all bounded-weight candidates through n=10.

value.rationale: The target parameter is an established domination invariant whose foundational paper proves hardness even on bipartite graphs. Crown graphs are a canonical dense regular bipartite family, and the theorem resolves not only the minimum weight but every minimum labeling and its exact multiplicity. The coordinate synchronization across deleted matching pairs is a structural phenomenon, and the n=3 exception shows the classification is not a routine restatement of the definition.
